newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end on plus note,small-caps extend rise.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end on plus note,small-caps extend rise.

text.p: Positive sentiment from Wall Street's 127-point surge, gains in some key Malaysian blue chips and year-end porfolio adjustments took share prices to a firmer finish.

"We're pretty much following Wall Street," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities. "In the last couple of weeks, there may be some window dressing in selective stocks."
Higher blue chips included Maybank, Telekom, Proton and Arab-Malaysian. But the Composite Index, which reached a high of 1,209.20 earlier, retraced to end at 1,203.06, up 2.03.
Volume expanded to 153 million shares, from 126 million on Thursday. Gainers outnumbered losers by 404 to 171.
"The Second Board is seeing a very minor bounce," said an institutional dealer with a local securities firm. "KFC looks like it's getting a bit of buying interest."

Stocks started the day stronger and generally held the firm tone throughout the session. But dealers were hard-pressed to find many interesting features ahead of the holidays. "I'm signing Christmas cards," said an equity analyst at a local firm.
